sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test setup and imports
sections.what: Imports the functions under test and a presence-check helper. Sets up one sample sentence about a nuclear project.
sections.why: Standard setup for the tests below.
sections.watch_out: Imports from two other folders, so moving those files breaks these tests.

sections.name: capture
sections.title: Tests for project attribution and source support
sections.what: Checks that a passage about another project is marked off-project, that a matching name without an exact source passage is absent, that inaccessible and stale pages are kept separate from absent evidence, that whitespace-only matches get no exact position, and that positions count special characters correctly. Also checks that numbers alone cannot verify a value.
sections.why: The test names state the rules.
sections.watch_out: The special-character test fixes an exact position, so any change to how positions are counted will break it.

sections.name: base
sections.title: Tests for money, date, status and name checks
sections.what: Checks that amounts, dates, status words and company names match only when the quote supports the exact meaning. Also checks overrun maths with zero, rejects forecasts and mismatched units, checks that a page names a project near a quote, and checks converted US dollar amounts.
sections.why: These tests guard the main rules that stop wrong numbers from being accepted.
sections.watch_out: These are the first tests to fail if a check is loosened, which is the intended behaviour.

summary: Automated tests for the evidence checks: whether a passage belongs to a project, whether a source supports a claim, whether money, dates and statuses mean what is claimed, and how cost overruns are calculated.
purpose: Protects the rules that decide whether a fact can be trusted.
why: The test names state each rule. The file has no separate comment about why.
how: Runs the assessment and field checks on fixed sample text, then asserts the expected result for each case. It contains about a dozen small tests.
inputs: Fixed sample text and values written inside the file.
outputs: A pass or fail for each test.
risks: The samples are fixed, so real wording that is not covered could still behave wrongly.
debug: Run this file and read the failing assertion. Compare its input text with the rule in evidence.ts or fieldSemantics.ts that it targets.
